title: Sentence adverbs in main and subordinate clauses
goal: Place ikke and common sentence adverbs correctly in main, subordinate, compound, and fronted clauses.

objectives.statement: Place ikke and common sentence adverbs correctly in main, subordinate, compound, and fronted clauses.

spans.value: Maja and Henrik are arranging a Saturday walk with their friend Sara. Rain is expected, and Sara has not answered their latest message yet.
Sara kommer ikke klokka ti. Hun må jobbe litt først.

blocks.translation: Sara isn’t coming at ten. She has to work a little first.

spans.value: Vet du om hun kommer senere?

blocks.translation: Do you know whether she is coming later?

spans.value: Hun skrev at hun kanskje kommer klokka tolv.

blocks.translation: She wrote that she might come at twelve.

spans.value: Jeg går vanligvis ikke på tur når det regner.

blocks.translation: I don’t usually go for a walk when it rains.

spans.value: Men det regner kanskje ikke hele dagen.

blocks.translation: But perhaps it won’t rain all day.

spans.value: Hvis det ikke regner klokka tolv, kan vi møte Sara ved stasjonen.

blocks.translation: If it isn’t raining at twelve, we can meet Sara at the station.

spans.value: Ja. Jeg sender henne en melding, men hun svarer aldri med en gang.

blocks.translation: Yes. I’ll send her a message, but she never answers immediately.

spans.value: Når hun endelig svarer, vet vi kanskje mer.

blocks.translation: When she finally answers, perhaps we’ll know more.

spans.value: The practical problem is simple: Maja and Henrik need to say what is not happening, what perhaps will happen, and what usually or never happens. To do that naturally, they must place words such as
because they affect the meaning of the whole statement or show the speaker’s attitude toward it. In this chapter, the important question is not which adverb to choose, but where to put it.
In the neutral declarative patterns taught here, word order changes according to the type of clause.

no.value: Sara kommer ikke klokka ti.

en.value: Sara isn’t coming at ten.

spans.value: is introduced by a word such as
and forms part of a larger sentence:

no.value: Maja sier at Sara ikke kommer klokka ti.

en.value: Maja says that Sara isn’t coming at ten.

spans.value: For the neutral declarative patterns taught here, the compact rule is:

statement.value: In a subject-first main clause, put the sentence adverb
. In a subordinate clause of the modeled type, put the sentence adverb

sections.title: Sentence adverbs in ordinary main clauses

spans.value: In a main clause beginning with the subject, the usual order is:
subject + finite verb + sentence adverb + rest

no.value: Sara kommer ikke klokka ti.

en.value: Sara isn’t coming at ten.

no.value: Hun svarer aldri med en gang.

en.value: She never answers immediately.

no.value: Vi går vanligvis langs elva.

en.value: We usually walk along the river.

no.value: Det regner kanskje i ettermiddag.

en.value: Perhaps it will rain this afternoon.

spans.value: When there is more than one verb, the sentence adverb still follows the finite verb and comes before the remaining verb form:

no.value: Sara kan ikke komme klokka ti.

en.value: Sara cannot come at ten.

no.value: Henrik vil kanskje vente på henne.

en.value: Henrik might wait for her.

no.value: Vi har aldri gått denne veien før.

en.value: We have never walked this way before.

spans.value: subject + finite verb + sentence adverb + other verb + rest

no.value: Sara kommer ikke.

en.value: Sara isn’t coming.

no.value: Sara kan ikke komme.

en.value: Sara cannot come.

spans.value: Learners sometimes copy English order and put
before the finite verb in an ordinary main clause.

no.value: ✗ Sara ikke kommer klokka ti.

en.value: Sara isn’t coming at ten.

no.value: Sara kommer ikke klokka ti.

en.value: Sara isn’t coming at ten.

spans.value: The incorrect order is not repaired by thinking only about the subject. First identify the finite verb; then place the sentence adverb after it.

no.value: Hun skrev at hun kanskje kommer klokka tolv.

en.value: She wrote that she might come at twelve.

no.value: at hun kanskje kommer klokka tolv

en.value: that she might come at twelve

spans.value: subordinator + subject + sentence adverb + finite verb + rest

no.value: Maja vet at Sara ikke kommer klokka ti.

en.value: Maja knows that Sara isn’t coming at ten.

no.value: Henrik tror at det kanskje regner senere.

en.value: Henrik thinks that perhaps it will rain later.

no.value: De blir hjemme fordi de vanligvis ikke går ut i kraftig regn.

en.value: They are staying home because they do not usually go out in heavy rain.

no.value: Maja spør om Sara aldri tar bussen.

en.value: Maja asks whether Sara never takes the bus.

spans.value: Again, in the neutral subordinate-clause pattern taught here, place the sentence adverb before the finite verb when the clause contains two verbs:

no.value: Maja vet at Sara ikke kan komme klokka ti.

en.value: Maja knows that Sara cannot come at ten.

no.value: Henrik tror at de kanskje må vente.

en.value: Henrik thinks that they may have to wait.

no.value: Sara sier at hun aldri har gått den veien.

en.value: Sara says that she has never walked that way.

spans.value: Compare the same idea in a main clause and a subordinate clause:

no.value: Sara kan ikke komme tidlig.

en.value: Sara cannot come early.

no.value: Maja vet at Sara ikke kan komme tidlig.

en.value: Maja knows that Sara cannot come early.

spans.value: . In the subordinate clause, it precedes
A long sentence can contain both clause types. Do not choose one adverb position for the entire sentence. Each clause has its own structure.

no.value: Henrik blir hjemme fordi han ikke liker regnet.

en.value: Henrik is staying home because he does not like the rain.

no.value: Henrik blir hjemme.

en.value: Henrik is staying home.

no.value: fordi han ikke liker regnet

en.value: because he does not like the rain

spans.value: is controlled by the subordinate clause in which it appears.
Sometimes a clause contains two relevant adverbs, as in Henrik’s statement:

no.value: Jeg går vanligvis ikke på tur når det regner.

en.value: I don’t usually go for a walk when it rains.

spans.value: makes the activity negative. In this meaning, the natural order is:

no.value: Jeg går vanligvis ikke på tur i regnet.

en.value: I don’t usually go for a walk in the rain.

spans.value: In a subordinate clause, both come before the finite verb:

no.value: Henrik sier at han vanligvis ikke går på tur i regnet.

en.value: Henrik says that he does not usually go for a walk in the rain.

no.value: Han går vanligvis ikke alene.

en.value: He does not usually walk alone.

no.value: fordi han vanligvis ikke går alene

en.value: because he does not usually walk alone

spans.value: The lesson contrast remains the same within these neutral patterns: sentence adverbs occur after the finite verb in the modeled main clauses and before it in the modeled subordinate clauses.
Do not infer that sentence adverbs can be placed in any order without changing the message. For now, learn common combinations as meaningful units, such as

sections.title: Compound sentences: check each clause separately

spans.value: joins coordinated main clauses, often with
. In the neutral subject-first examples here, each part follows the modeled main-clause word order.

no.value: Jeg sender henne en melding, men hun svarer aldri med en gang.

en.value: I’ll send her a message, but she never answers immediately.

no.value: hun svarer aldri med en gang

en.value: she never answers immediately

spans.value: It therefore has finite verb + sentence adverb:

no.value: Sara kommer ikke klokka ti, men hun kommer kanskje klokka tolv.

en.value: Sara isn’t coming at ten, but she may come at twelve.

no.value: Vi tar ikke bussen, og Henrik kjører heller ikke.

en.value: We aren’t taking the bus, and Henrik isn’t driving either.

no.value: Maja har aldri gått denne ruten, men Henrik kjenner den godt.

en.value: Maja has never walked this route, but Henrik knows it well.

spans.value: A conjunction does not automatically create a subordinate clause. After
, a complete second main clause keeps main-clause order.

no.value: Sara kommer ikke fordi hun må jobbe.

en.value: Sara isn’t coming because she has to work.

spans.value: Now add a sentence adverb there:

no.value: Sara kommer ikke fordi hun ikke har tid.

en.value: Sara isn’t coming because she does not have time.

spans.value: Common misconception: every linking word works alike
as the same kind of connector. They are not.

no.value: Hun kommer ikke, men hun ringer kanskje.

en.value: She isn’t coming, but she may call.

no.value: Hun kommer ikke fordi hun kanskje må jobbe.

en.value: She isn’t coming because she may have to work.

spans.value: , the second clause is a main clause, so
A main clause does not always begin with the subject. A time, place, or other element can be moved to the front:

no.value: I dag kommer Sara ikke klokka ti.

en.value: Today Sara isn’t coming at ten.

spans.value: When something other than the subject occupies the first position, the finite verb comes next. With an unstressed pronoun subject, the neutral pattern taught here places the subject before the sentence adverb. With a full noun subject, sentence-adverb placement relative to the subject can vary with information structure; the examples below model one common order without excluding supported alternatives:
fronted element + finite verb + unstressed pronoun subject + sentence adverb + rest

no.value: I dag kommer Sara ikke klokka ti.

en.value: Today Sara isn’t coming at ten.

no.value: På lørdager går Henrik vanligvis langs elva.

en.value: On Saturdays Henrik usually walks along the river.

no.value: Etter jobb kan Sara kanskje møte dem.

en.value: After work, Sara might be able to meet them.

no.value: Denne veien har Maja aldri gått før.

en.value: Maja has never walked this way before.

spans.value: Compare the ordinary and fronted versions:

no.value: Sara kommer ikke klokka ti i dag.

en.value: Sara isn’t coming at ten today.

no.value: I dag kommer Sara ikke klokka ti.

en.value: Today Sara isn’t coming at ten.

spans.value: The sentence adverb remains connected to the finite-verb area, but fronting changes the positions of the finite verb and subject.
A frequent mistake is to keep subject-first order after a fronted element:

no.value: ✗ I dag Sara kommer ikke klokka ti.

en.value: Today Sara isn’t coming at ten.

no.value: I dag kommer Sara ikke klokka ti.

en.value: Today Sara isn’t coming at ten.

spans.value: , both of these orders can be accepted, depending on information structure and context:

no.value: I dag kommer ikke Sara klokka ti.

en.value: Today Sara isn’t coming at ten.

no.value: I dag kommer Sara ikke klokka ti.

en.value: Today Sara isn’t coming at ten.

spans.value: This lesson models the second order but does not treat the first as necessarily contrastive or incorrect. For deterministic placement practice, use an unstressed pronoun subject, as in
I dag kommer hun ikke klokka ti
A subordinate clause can itself come first:

no.value: Hvis det ikke regner klokka tolv, kan vi møte Sara ved stasjonen.

en.value: If it isn’t raining at twelve, we can meet Sara at the station.

spans.value: This sentence contains two word-order decisions.

no.value: hvis det ikke regner klokka tolv

en.value: if it isn’t raining at twelve

spans.value: subordinator + subject + sentence adverb + finite verb

no.value: kan vi møte Sara ved stasjonen

en.value: we can meet Sara at the station

spans.value: Because the subordinate clause occupies the first position of the whole sentence, the following main clause begins with its finite verb:
fronted subordinate clause + finite verb + subject + rest
If the following main clause contains an unstressed pronoun subject and a sentence adverb, the neutral pattern taught here places the adverb after that subject:

no.value: Hvis det ikke regner, kan vi kanskje gå langs elva.

en.value: If it isn’t raining, perhaps we can walk along the river.

no.value: Når Sara endelig svarer, vet vi kanskje mer.

en.value: When Sara finally answers, perhaps we’ll know more.

no.value: Fordi Henrik ikke liker kraftig regn, går han vanligvis ikke langt.

en.value: Because Henrik does not like heavy rain, he does not usually walk far.

no.value: Hvis Sara ikke kan komme, blir Maja kanskje hjemme.

en.value: If Sara cannot come, Maja may stay home.

no.value: Når de ikke tar bussen, går de vanligvis fra stasjonen.

en.value: When they do not take the bus, they usually walk from the station.

spans.value: Do not move the subordinate-clause adverb merely because the whole subordinate clause has been moved. Its internal order stays subordinate:

no.value: fordi Henrik ikke liker regn

en.value: because Henrik does not like rain

no.value: Fordi Henrik ikke liker regn, blir han hjemme.

en.value: Because Henrik does not like rain, he stays home.

spans.value: Fronting changes the relationship between the opening clause and the following main clause. It does not turn the opening subordinate clause into a main clause.

spans.value: Jeg kan dessverre ikke komme klokka tolv.

blocks.translation: Unfortunately, I can’t come at twelve.

spans.value: Jeg vet ikke om jeg kan dra tidlig fra jobb.

blocks.translation: I don’t know whether I can leave work early.

spans.value: Hvis du ikke kan komme i dag, kan vi kanskje gå på tur i morgen.

spans.value: Det passer bra. På søndager jobber jeg vanligvis ikke.

blocks.translation: That works well. On Sundays I don’t usually work.

spans.value: For the neutral declarative patterns practiced in this lesson, work through these decisions:

items.value: Find the clause containing the adverb.
Decide whether the clause is a main clause or a subordinate clause.
In the modeled subordinate-clause pattern, place the sentence adverb before the finite verb.
In the modeled subject-first main-clause pattern, place it after the finite verb.

If another element or a subordinate clause comes first, keep main-clause verb-second order. With an unstressed pronoun subject, use finite verb + subject + sentence adverb; with a full noun subject, allow supported variation according to information structure.

spans.value: Use the contrast as your memory aid:

en.value: Sara cannot come.

en.value: because Sara cannot come

no.value: I dag kan Sara ikke komme.

en.value: Today Sara cannot come.

no.value: Hvis Sara ikke kan komme, kan Maja kanskje møte Henrik.

en.value: If Sara cannot come, perhaps Maja can meet Henrik.

sections.title: Cumulative transfer: planning a weekday dinner

spans.value: Imagine that Nora and Jonas are planning dinner with Emil after work. Emil may be late, Nora does not usually eat after nine, and Jonas has never visited the chosen restaurant.

Without looking back, write four short Norwegian sentences about a changed plan: one ordinary subject-first main clause with a target sentence adverb; one complete sentence with a target sentence adverb inside an unfronted subordinate clause introduced by

; one compound sentence with a target sentence adverb in each coordinated main clause; and one sentence with a target sentence adverb inside the opening fronted subordinate clause and another in the following main clause. Use at least three of

; you may reuse an adverb where needed. Successful retrieval shows the practiced sentence-adverb placement in every clause named above. Use unstressed pronoun subjects where a fronted main-clause portion is evaluated for one fixed order.

prompt.value: Select the correctly ordered verb group in each main clause. Each blank contains the finite verb, any other verb, and one sentence adverb. Choose the option that places the adverb after the finite verb.

explanation.value: In main clauses the sentence adverb follows the finite verb; in subordinate clauses it precedes the finite verb.

prompt.value: In each pair, choose the correctly ordered verb group. The first sentence is an independent main clause; the second is inside a subordinate clause. Place the sentence adverb after the finite verb in the main clause and before it in the subordinate clause.

explanation.value: Ikke follows the finite verb in the main clause but precedes it in the subordinate clause.

prompt.value: Build one complete longer dinner-plan sentence from all supplied tokens. It must combine Emil's arrival, the restaurant, and the group's decision with men and fordi. Keep sentence-adverb placement correct in every clause.

Build the dinner-plan sentence from all supplied tokens so that the subordinate clause comes first. Keep ikke before the finite verb in that clause and place kanskje after the pronoun subject in the following main clause.

Write four short, natural Norwegian messages about Nora, Jonas, and Emil planning dinner. Use full clauses, not isolated fragments, and use each of ikke, aldri, vanligvis, and kanskje exactly once. Message 1 must be an ordinary subject-first main clause saying that Emil may arrive after work, with kanskje. Message 2 must be a complete sentence containing a fordi subordinate clause saying that Emil is not coming, with ikke in that subordinate clause. Message 3 must be an ordinary subject-first main clause saying that Nora never eats after nine, with aldri. Message 4 must be a complete sentence containing an om subordinate clause asking whether Jonas usually wants to eat at the restaurant, with vanligvis in that subordinate clause. Keep the intended practical meanings.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the four requested messages and report evidence for every criterion. Mark a criterion unmet when the required meaning, clause type, or adverb placement is not observable.

criteria.instruction: Provides four complete natural Norwegian messages matching the four requested dinner meanings, not isolated fragments.
Uses ikke, aldri, vanligvis, and kanskje exactly once each.
Places the adverb after the finite verb in the ordinary subject-first main clauses in messages 1 and 3.
Places the adverb before the finite verb in the fordi subordinate clause in message 2 and the om subordinate clause in message 4.

prompt.value: Write exactly four short Norwegian sentences about a changed plan, using your own details. Sentence 1 must be an ordinary subject-first main clause with a target sentence adverb. Sentence 2 must be a complete sentence with a target sentence adverb inside an unfronted subordinate clause introduced by at, fordi, hvis, or om. Sentence 3 must be a compound sentence with a target sentence adverb in each coordinated main clause. Sentence 4 must begin with a fronted subordinate clause containing one target sentence adverb and must have another target sentence adverb in the following main clause. Use at least three of ikke, aldri, vanligvis, and kanskje. In sentence 4, use an unstressed pronoun subject in the following main clause.

payload.judge_prompt: Check exactly four sentences against the task and report evidence for every criterion. Mark a criterion unmet when the required clause structure or sentence-adverb placement is missing or ambiguous.

criteria.instruction: Sentence 1 is an ordinary subject-first main clause with the target adverb after the finite verb.
Sentence 2 contains an unfronted subordinate clause introduced by an approved connector with the target adverb before its finite verb.
Sentence 3 has two coordinated main clauses and places a target adverb after the finite verb in each clause.
Sentence 4 has a fronted subordinate clause with its adverb before the finite verb and a following main clause with the sequence finite verb, unstressed pronoun subject, and adverb.
Uses at least three distinct target adverbs and gives original changed-plan content rather than copying a lesson example.
